Description: Allows a Moderator to find and open work that requires human review: pending publication submissions and unresolved content reports. The queue is an operational view; opening or filtering an item does not decide it.
Trigger: The Moderator opens the moderation workspace or follows a moderation notification.
Preconditions: 1. The user is authenticated. 2. The user has an active Moderator role. 3. NovelHub can read the current moderation records.
Postconditions: The queue is displayed with current statuses. If an item is selected, its current review record is opened. No publication or report outcome is changed.
Normal Flow: 1. NovelHub loads pending submissions and unresolved reports. 2. The system shows item type, submitted/reported time, current status and available risk indicators. 3. The Moderator filters or sorts by work type, status, date or risk. 4. The Moderator selects a submission for UC-MOD-02 or a report for UC-MOD-04. 5. NovelHub rechecks that the selected record is still open before displaying it.
Alternative Flows: A1. If the queue is empty, NovelHub displays an empty state without treating it as an error. A2. If AI evidence is pending or unavailable, the item remains visible with that status; it is not silently hidden. A3. If another Moderator has already completed the item, NovelHub refreshes the status and prevents a stale decision.
Exception Flows: E1. If authentication expires or Moderator permission is revoked, access is denied. E2. If the queue cannot be loaded, NovelHub displays a recoverable error and does not alter moderation records.
Business Rules: Only open work appears as actionable. AI risk indicators can support prioritization but cannot decide publication or report outcomes. Admin finance and account-governance work must not appear as Moderator work.

Supporting Actors / Systems: OpenAI LLM Service; OpenAI Embedding Service; VPSTTT Object Storage
Description: Allows a Moderator to evaluate the exact story or chapter revision submitted by an Author using the content, formatting state, rights declaration, media, AI review results and similarity findings available for that revision.
Trigger: The Moderator opens a pending publication submission from UC-MOD-01.
Preconditions: 1. The Moderator is authorized. 2. The submission is pending review. 3. The submitted revision is identifiable and has not been replaced by a newer revision. 4. Required submission metadata and rights declaration exist.
Postconditions: The reviewed revision and available evidence have been displayed. The submission remains pending until UC-MOD-03 records a decision.
Normal Flow: 1. NovelHub displays the exact submitted story/chapter revision and its metadata. 2. The Moderator checks structure, formatting and media availability. 3. The Moderator reviews the Author's rights/license declaration. 4. NovelHub displays automatic AI review results and risk flags. 5. NovelHub displays similarity findings with source/context information available to the system. 6. The Moderator inspects relevant content and evidence rather than accepting a score alone. 7. The Moderator records review notes when needed. 8. The Moderator proceeds to UC-MOD-03.
Alternative Flows: A1. If AI review is still processing, the Moderator may wait, return later or continue with clearly marked incomplete evidence according to policy. A2. If AI/embedding services failed, NovelHub shows the failure status; it does not invent a clean result. A3. A high similarity score prompts contextual review of quoted, licensed, public-domain or independently created material. A4. A resubmitted revision starts a new review context and must not inherit a decision from the older revision.
Exception Flows: E1. If the submitted revision changed or was withdrawn while open, NovelHub blocks a stale decision and reloads the current state. E2. If required content/media cannot be retrieved, the submission remains pending and the missing evidence is shown. E3. If access to the record is unauthorized, NovelHub denies access and records no review action.
Business Rules: AI output is advisory. Similarity is a risk signal, not a legal plagiarism verdict. Rights declarations are evidence, not automatic proof. A moderation decision must apply to the exact revision reviewed.
Related Requirements: FR-AUTHOR-13 through FR-AUTHOR-16; FR-MOD-02 through FR-MOD-06; FR-MOD-08; FR-MOD-11; FR-MEDIA-03; BR-11 through BR-13

Description: Allows a Moderator to approve, reject or request revision for the exact submitted revision after human review, with a reasoned decision and durable audit record.
Trigger: The Moderator completes UC-MOD-02 and chooses to decide the pending submission.
Preconditions: 1. The Moderator is authorized. 2. The submission is still pending. 3. The exact reviewed revision is unchanged. 4. Required review evidence has been presented or any unavailable evidence is explicitly marked.
Postconditions: The submission status becomes approved, rejected or revision requested. The decision, Moderator, timestamp, reviewed revision and reason/feedback are retained. The Author can see the updated status and feedback.
Normal Flow: 1. NovelHub shows the current revision and a decision form. 2. The Moderator selects Approve, Reject or Request Revision. 3. For Reject or Request Revision, the Moderator provides actionable reasons; an approval note is optional unless policy requires it. 4. NovelHub validates that the submission is still pending and unchanged. 5. NovelHub records the decision atomically with the reviewed revision, Moderator identity, timestamp and feedback. 6. NovelHub updates the publication/review status. 7. NovelHub makes the result available to the Author and attempts the configured notification. 8. The decision appears in moderation history.
Alternative Flows: A1. Approve: the content becomes approved/published according to the publication workflow. A2. Reject: the submission is closed as rejected and the Author receives the reason. A3. Request Revision: the submission returns to the Author with required changes; a later resubmission creates a new review cycle and automatic AI review. A4. Notification delivery failure is recorded but does not roll back a valid decision.
Exception Flows: E1. If another Moderator already decided the submission, NovelHub rejects the stale action and shows the current status. E2. If the Author withdrew or replaced the revision, NovelHub blocks the decision. E3. If the decision cannot be stored, NovelHub leaves the submission pending and must not send a success notification.
Business Rules: Only a Moderator makes the final routine publication decision. AI never auto-approves or auto-rejects. Reject and revision outcomes require meaningful feedback. Existing decision history is retained rather than overwritten.
Related Requirements: FR-AUTHOR-16; FR-MOD-07 through FR-MOD-10; FR-NOTIFY-03; FR-NOTIFY-04; BR-11; BR-13

Description: Allows a Moderator to inspect a Reader report together with the reported content, report reason, available context and related moderation evidence before choosing an outcome.
Trigger: The Moderator opens an unresolved report from UC-MOD-01.
Preconditions: 1. The Moderator is authorized. 2. The report is unresolved. 3. The report identifies its target content and reason. 4. NovelHub can retrieve the content or can show that it is unavailable.
Postconditions: The report and available context have been reviewed. No enforcement action occurs until UC-MOD-05 records the resolution.
Normal Flow: 1. NovelHub displays the report category, reason, submitted evidence and target content. 2. The system displays the current publication/content state and the exact content reference associated with the report. 3. The Moderator reviews surrounding context needed to avoid judging an isolated fragment incorrectly. 4. The Moderator checks related reports and relevant prior moderation history. 5. The Moderator compares the content against platform rules and the available rights/review evidence. 6. The Moderator records review notes when needed. 7. The Moderator proceeds to UC-MOD-05.
Alternative Flows: A1. Multiple reports about the same content may be reviewed together while retaining each original report record. A2. If the content was already removed or unpublished, NovelHub shows the prior action and allows the Moderator to resolve the remaining report consistently. A3. If evidence is insufficient, the Moderator may leave the report open for later review rather than guessing. A4. A report that does not establish a violation can proceed to dismissal.
Exception Flows: E1. If the target was deleted or cannot be retrieved, NovelHub preserves report metadata and shows the unavailable state. E2. If the report is resolved concurrently, NovelHub prevents a second conflicting resolution. E3. If Moderator authorization is lost, no report action is recorded.
Business Rules: A report is an allegation, not proof. The Moderator must review context before acting. Reporter and user data shown to the Moderator is limited to information authorized for moderation. Account-role changes and financial sanctions remain Admin responsibilities.

Description: Allows a Moderator to dismiss a report or apply a permitted content action, record the reason and close the report without silently erasing its history.
Trigger: After UC-MOD-04, the Moderator selects a report resolution.
Preconditions: 1. The Moderator is authorized. 2. The report is still unresolved. 3. The target content and available evidence have been reviewed. 4. The requested action is within Moderator permissions.
Postconditions: The report has a recorded resolution. If a content action was selected, the content state reflects that action. The resolution, reason, Moderator, timestamp and affected content revision are retained in moderation history.
Normal Flow: 1. NovelHub presents permitted outcomes for the report. 2. The Moderator selects Dismiss/No Violation or a permitted content action. 3. The Moderator provides a resolution reason. 4. NovelHub rechecks report and content state. 5. NovelHub records the resolution and any content-state change consistently. 6. The system closes the report and links related actions/history. 7. NovelHub makes required feedback/status available to affected users and attempts configured notifications. 8. The result appears in moderation history.
Alternative Flows: A1. No violation: the report is dismissed with a reason and content remains unchanged. A2. Correctable issue: the Moderator applies the configured restriction or requests correction when that action is supported. A3. Confirmed violation: NovelHub applies an authorized action such as hiding or unpublishing the affected content. A4. Duplicate reports can be closed by reference to the same underlying action while retaining separate report records. A5. Notification failure is recorded without undoing the moderation outcome.
Exception Flows: E1. If another Moderator resolves the report first, NovelHub rejects the stale action and reloads the current resolution. E2. If the content action fails, NovelHub must not falsely mark the report as successfully enforced; it records a recoverable failure/pending state. E3. If the selected action exceeds Moderator permission, NovelHub rejects it without changing content.
Business Rules: Every resolution requires an auditable reason. Moderator actions are limited to permitted content moderation; user-account/role governance belongs to Admin. Resolution history is retained. Similarity or AI flags alone are insufficient proof of a violation.
Related Requirements: FR-MOD-08 through FR-MOD-11; FR-NOTIFY-03; FR-NOTIFY-04; BR-11; BR-12

Description: Allows a Moderator to inspect prior publication decisions, report resolutions and content actions for consistency, context and auditability without changing historical records.
Trigger: The Moderator opens moderation history directly or follows a history link from a submission, report or content item.
Preconditions: 1. The Moderator is authorized. 2. At least the history view is available; matching records may or may not exist.
Postconditions: Matching history is displayed. No submission, report, content state or historical record is modified.
Normal Flow: 1. NovelHub displays available moderation records. 2. The Moderator filters by content, Author, action type, outcome, date or status. 3. The Moderator opens a record. 4. NovelHub shows the reviewed content/revision reference, decision or action, reason/feedback, Moderator, timestamp and evidence references that were retained. 5. The Moderator may navigate back to the current submission, report or content record when authorized.
Alternative Flows: A1. If no records match, NovelHub displays an empty result. A2. If linked media/content is no longer available, the retained audit metadata remains visible with an unavailable indicator. A3. If a historical record has a later corrective action, NovelHub shows both records in chronological order rather than replacing the earlier one.
Exception Flows: E1. Unauthorized filters or records are not disclosed. E2. If history retrieval fails, NovelHub displays an error and does not alter records. E3. Missing linked objects do not cause the history record itself to disappear.
Business Rules: Moderation history is read-only through this use case. Decisions and actions must remain attributable to the Moderator and reviewed revision. Corrections create additional history rather than silently rewriting past outcomes.
